lines.text: You are taller when you wake up than when you go to bed.
Every day you shrink, and every night you grow back.
Between the bones of your spine sit soft discs, full of water.
Standing and walking all day squeezes water out of them, and they flatten.
Lying down at night lets them soak it back up.
The difference is roughly a centimetre, and in children it can be even more.
In space it's extreme. Without gravity, astronauts can grow up to 3% taller.
It wears off within months of coming back to Earth.
So if you ever want to be measured at your tallest, do it first thing in the morning.

sources.claim: Height drops during the day as intervertebral discs lose fluid; mean 10.8 mm daily loss measured in adolescents
Children lost a mean 31 mm between morning and afternoon (Voss and Bailey)
Astronauts can grow up to 3% taller in microgravity, returning to normal within months

publish.title: You Shrink Every Single Day 📏
publish.description: You're taller in the morning than at night, and astronauts get up to 3% taller in space. Here's what your spine is doing.
